references.text: The Pharisees and the teachers of the law ask Jesus for a sign, which corresponds to the demand in Luke 11:16 for a sign from heaven.
The Pharisees and Sadducees come to Jesus and test him by asking for a sign from heaven—the same motive as in Luke 11:16.
The Pharisees come and begin to argue with Jesus, demanding a sign from heaven to test him (πειράζοντες), directly parallel to Luke 11:16.
The crowd asks Jesus for a sign they can see so that they may believe in him—the same demand for visible confirmation from heaven.
Paul writes that the Jews demand signs—this summarizes the attitude we see in Luke 11:16, where some demand heavenly signs from Jesus.
Jesus calls that generation an evil and unfaithful people who demand a sign, saying that the only sign they will receive is the sign of Jonah—Jesus' answer to the demand in Luke 11:16.
Jesus' response to the demand for a sign follows immediately in the same context: this generation is an evil generation that demands signs, but only the sign of Jonah will be given.
The command not to test the Lord your God (which Jesus himself quotes in Matt 4:7)—those who demand signs from heaven to test Jesus are putting God to the test.
